log.memory: I am Gilbert Ashe, head of the Ashes of Holloway, partnered with Edith (she also fells and burns charcoal). I am a master at felling timber, burning charcoal, making packs and making handcarts. I carry a crude tool (it doubles felling: about 4.4 timber for 2 units) and a handcart (40 weight on a cart track, 10 off-track). I also have 8 coin. Summer days 3-5 (summer has 8 days): I felled timber, burned charcoal and taught Rose Rook charcoal burning. She paid in firewood for the Ashe store and now has the craft. At the end of day 5 I carried about 4 charcoal, 0.6 meat, a hide, 0.4 wild food and about 4 timber. Ashe House store at day 5: 3.7 charcoal, 1.3 dried meat, 22 firewood, 6.6 grain, very little timber. Food was about 8.7 meals, and two of us eat about 2 a night, so FOOD IS RUNNING LOW. I need to hunt, forage, trade for grain or bread, or work the harvest. Our two oat fields (the Hill Field and the Lower Field) are sown and growing, so I should weed them and reap at harvest. Holloway: the Coppice and Holloway Hanger have plenty of timber, firewood and wild food. Holloway Hanger has game (I heard something heavy in the undergrowth at dusk). The Glade has hay and a spring. Our neighbours the Rooks are Denise, Rose and Simkin. Trade plan: carry charcoal by handcart along the cart track through the Weald (1 day) to Wynford (1 more day). Wynford's market is every 8th day, on the Green. There I can trade charcoal for grain or barley and use the Wynns' mill (they keep a share of the grain). Harvest farms pay reapers in grain. Stannick (cheese, rye, stone) is 2 days from Wynford by cart track. Winter: a hearth needs about 16 timber (or 64 firewood) to see a house through the cold. Last winter was hard and the stores ran out, so stock fuel and food (dried meat or bread for travel). Debts: Wilmot Cotter (Wynford) owes me 1 meat from last winter, in arrears (agreement A20). I should collect it at Wynford. Family: our daughters Katherine and Joan married into Ashby, 2 days away. I have named no heir. Lore: rye stands the winter, but barley sown after mid-autumn won't ripen. Whoever clears and sows ground holds it. There are unexplored ways: the deer path north to a deep dene and high grazing, the old pass over the Tor, and an old holloway from the Weald to an unseen lake. Our creed: cut and burn, carry and sell, keep your word and your accounts.

I am Gilbert Ashe, head of the Ashes of Holloway, partnered with Edith (she also fells, burns charcoal, hunts and reaps). I am a master at felling timber, burning charcoal, making packs and making handcarts. I carry a crude tool, which doubles felling (about 4.4 timber for 2 units; charcoal needs 5 timber, so fell twice before burning), and a handcart (40 weight on a cart track, 10 off-track). I have 8 coin. End of summer (day 8): I carry about 4.7 charcoal, 8.3 grain (reaped from our oat fields: Hill Field 3.8, Lower Field 4.5), 0.1 dried meat and a hide. Ashe House store: about 24 firewood (or more, since Rose keeps adding), 6.5 grain, 4.4 timber, NO charcoal and no dried meat. Edith carries plenty of charcoal, some timber and some grain. FOOD IS LOW. Grain is only 0.2 a meal raw but 0.7 at a lit fire, so eat it at home or bring timber to light a fire on the road. Two of us eat about 2 a night. Lessons: there is NO hand mill at Ashe House, so I cannot grind flour or bake bread. A hand mill needs 2 stone, which can be got at High Tor or Stannick (quarrying needs a tool). My hunts at Holloway Hanger failed 3 times running and the wild food there is used up, so don't count on hunting. You cannot travel from Holloway straight to Wynford: travel to "the Weald" first (1 day, cart track), then to Wynford (1 more day). Plan only actions I can actually do, because refused actions waste units. Rose Rook: I taught her charcoal burning (summer), and on summer day 8 I gave her a day's lesson in handcart making, so she should be capable now. She pays in firewood to the Ashe store and is a good neighbour. Simkin Rook left on a journey with a bedroll on summer day 6. The Rooks are Denise, Rose and Simkin. Plan for autumn: go to Wynford by way of the Weald with charcoal to trade for grain, flour or bread at the market (every 8th day, on the Green). The Wynns grind anyone's grain at their Mill for a share, so I could take our grain there to be milled into flour. Harvest farms pay reapers in grain. Collect the 1 meat Wilmot Cotter owes me (A20, in arrears). Stannick (cheese, rye, stone, cattle) is 2 days from Wynford by cart track. Westmere is 1 day from Wynford. Also try to get stone for a hand mill. Before I leave, put grain into the store for Edith if she needs it. Winter: a hearth needs about 16 timber (or 64 firewood) to see a house through the cold. Last winter was hard and the stores ran out, so stock fuel and food (dried meat or bread for travel). Rye stands the winter, but barley sown after mid-autumn won't ripen. Whoever clears and sows ground holds it. Holloway: the Clearing (Ashe House, Rook House) is next to the Coppice, the Hill Field and the Glade. The Coppice (timber, firewood) is next to Holloway Hanger (timber, firewood, game) on the hilltop. The roads to High Tor and the deer path north leave from the Hanger, and the road to the Weald leaves from the Clearing. The Glade has hay and a spring. Family: our daughters Katherine and Joan married into Ashby, 2 days away. I have named no heir. Unexplored ways: the deer path north to a deep dene and high grazing, the old pass over the Tor, and an old holloway from the Weald to an unseen lake. Our creed: cut and burn, carry and sell, keep your word and your accounts.

I am Gilbert Ashe, head of the Ashes of Holloway, partnered with Edith (she also fells, burns charcoal, hunts and reaps). I am a master at felling timber, burning charcoal, making packs and making handcarts. I carry a crude tool, which doubles felling (about 4.4 timber for 2 units; charcoal needs 5 timber, so fell twice before burning), and a handcart (40 weight on a cart track, 10 off it). I have 8 coin. I have named no heir. WHERE I AM (autumn day 3, day 9 of these days): I left the Weald for Wynford and arrive on the morning of autumn day 4 (day 10). I carry 12.7 charcoal (our trade stock, partly from Edith), a hide, and very little food (about 0.3 wild food), so I must trade for food or find a host quickly. Edith asked me to get dried meat and cheese, and to have grain milled at the Wynns' Mill (they keep a share for the grinding). Harvest farms pay reapers in grain, so that is another way to earn food. Wynford's market is every 8th day on the Green, but I am not sure which day it falls on, so ask. I must collect the 1 meat Wilmot Cotter owes me (A20, in arrears). Try to get 2 stone for a hand mill too (from Stannick or High Tor; quarrying needs a tool). Stannick (cheese, rye, stone, cattle) is 2 days from Wynford by cart track. Westmere is 1 day from Wynford. HOME (when I left on autumn day 1): Ashe House is sound, with 5 beds, a hearth and bins, but NO hand mill. Its store holds about 29.9 grain, 25.3 firewood, 5.8 timber and 2.3 straw. Both oat fields are reaped. Edith is at home. THE ROOKS (Denise, Rose, Simkin) are good neighbours. Rose is now capable at charcoal burning and handcart making (I taught her both). She pays in firewood, and she reaped 2 units of the Hill Field to square the lesson. Denise offers to reap for about 4 grain a day. Simkin keeps Rook camp at Weald Edge (4 beds, a fire ring, some firewood in its store). He lets me sleep there on my way back. He has 3 coin and wants to know Wynford's grain and bread prices. Tell him those on the way back. Also give Rose his message: a handcart would let them haul timber and meat from the Weald along the cart track, and the camp sleeps four. ROUTES: Holloway to the Weald is 1 day by cart track (a spring on the way), and the Weald to Wynford is 1 more day by cart track. There is no direct road from Holloway to Wynford. The Weald has Weald Edge and the Heart of the Weald, with plentiful timber, firewood and deer slots. But my hunts keep failing (4 times now) and the wild food there is picked over, so it gives only about 1 wild food per forage. Don't count on hunting. LESSONS: Grain is only 0.2 a meal raw but 0.7 at a lit fire. On the road, carry bread or dried meat, or carry timber and use "fire". A night out costs 1.5 food (2 if cold). Plan only actions I can actually do, because refused actions waste units. Don't leave units idle: fell or forage instead of resting.

I am Gilbert Ashe, head of the Ashes of Holloway, partnered with Edith (she also fells, burns charcoal, hunts and reaps). I am a master at felling timber, burning charcoal, making packs and making handcarts. I carry a crude tool, which doubles felling (about 4.4 timber for 2 units). Charcoal needs 5 timber, so I fell twice before burning. I also have a handcart (40 weight on a cart track, 10 off it). I have named no heir. WHERE I AM: I left the Weald with Simkin on autumn day 6 and we arrive at Holloway on the morning of autumn day 7 (day 13). Winter is close. I carry 6.7 charcoal, 8 coin, 15.2 grain, the crude tool, the handcart, a hide and 0.5 straw. PROMISE TO KEEP: Simkin will give 3 coin for 6 grain delivered to Rook House. We agreed it by word only, with no formal offer yet. At Holloway I should make him the offer, or give the grain into the Rook House store and take his coin. Also give Rose Simkin's message: a handcart would let them haul timber and meat from the Weald along the cart track, and the camp sleeps four. Rook camp at Weald Edge (4 beds, a fire ring) stays open to the Ashes whenever we pass. WYNFORD TRIP (autumn days 4-5): Warin Wynn traded me 20 grain for 6 charcoal, so grain there is about 3.3 for 1 charcoal. The Wynns and Cotters have grain to spare after harvest. I reaped 8.1 grain at Fallow Close, thinking that by custom reapers are paid in grain. But that field's harvest was under a Wynn-Cotter agreement (two parts to the Cotters, one part to the Wynns), and Warin asked where my grain went. I offered to make it right, and I left 4 grain on the Green (only to lighten my load), but it was never settled with him. Next visit, make it right with Warin so my name stays good. LESSON: before reaping someone else's field, agree the pay first. I never got the dried meat, the cheese, the milling or the stone that Edith asked for. Richard Moor of Stannick offered 6 coin for a copper tool, so copper tools are worth a lot. I did not learn bread prices, and I still don't know which day Wynford's market falls on. DEBTS: Wilmot Cotter owes me 1 meat (A20, in arrears). He promised it by the end of autumn, so collect it when we meet. HOME (when I left on autumn day 1): Ashe House is sound, with 5 beds, a hearth and bins, but NO hand mill. A hand mill needs 2 stone, from Stannick or High Tor, and quarrying needs a tool. The store held about 29.9 grain, 25.3 firewood, 5.8 timber and 2.3 straw. Both oat fields are reaped, and Edith is at home. A hearth needs about 16 timber, or 64 firewood, for the winter, so lay in more fuel: fell and gather firewood at Holloway or the Weald. Building bins or beds and repairs need timber. THE ROOKS (Denise, Rose, Simkin) are good neighbours. Rose is capable at charcoal burning and handcart making (I taught her both). She pays in firewood. Denise reaps for about 4 grain a day. Simkin had 3 coin. ROUTES: Holloway to the Weald is 1 day by cart track (a spring on the way), and the Weald to Wynford is 1 more day by cart track.

I am Gilbert Ashe, head of the Ashes of Holloway. My partner is Edith; she also fells, burns charcoal, hunts and reaps. I am a master at felling timber, burning charcoal, making packs and making handcarts, and I am competent at hunting. I have named no heir. MY BIGGEST MISTAKE (fix it first): To put things INTO the house store I must use move with "to": "store" at Ashe House. "to": "hands" takes things OUT of the store. For three days I kept pulling grain and straw out of the store instead of putting my load in, and I wasted my units doing it. TOOL LOST: My crude tool is gone; it probably broke. Without it, felling gives only about 1.1 timber for 2 units, and I cannot cut young growth at all. Make a new crude tool soon. With a tool I get about 4.4 timber for 2 units. WHERE I AM (end of winter day 1, day 15): At home in Holloway, snow and cold. I carry 7.7 charcoal, 8 coin (maybe 11 if Simkin's 3 coin reached me), about 12.2 grain, the handcart, a hide, 4 straw and 11.7 timber. That is far too heavy: put the timber, charcoal, hide, straw and spare grain into the Ashe House store. ASHE HOUSE: Sound, 5 beds, a hearth, bins, but NO hand mill. The store holds about 42.6 grain, about 18 firewood, 15 straw and NO timber. On a cold winter night the hearth burns 4 heat, which is 8 firewood or 2 timber. Fuel is urgent: put my timber in the store and keep felling and gathering firewood. Charcoal burns at 6 heat a unit, so it can heat the house in an emergency. A hand mill needs 2 stone from Stannick or High Tor, and quarrying needs a tool. SETTLED: Simkin gave 3 coin for the 6 grain I left at Rook House. That deal is done and my word is kept. The Rooks (Denise, Rose, Simkin) are all home and are good neighbours. Rose is capable at burning charcoal and making handcarts (I taught her both), and she pays in firewood. Denise reaps for about 4 grain a day. Rook camp at Weald Edge (4 beds, a fire ring) is open to the Ashes whenever we pass. Simkin knows something of striking coin. Rose wants to know when the market is, and to ask for news there. WYNFORD: Warin Wynn traded me 20 grain for 6 charcoal, so grain there runs about 3.3 for 1 charcoal. The Wynns and Cotters had grain to spare after harvest. UNSETTLED: I reaped 8.1 grain at Fallow Close, which was under a Wynn-Cotter harvest agreement. Next visit, make it right with Warin. (I told Edith I left 4 grain on the Green to settle it, but it was never really settled.) LESSON: agree the pay before reaping someone else's field. I still don't know which day the market falls on, or what bread costs. Edith wanted dried meat, cheese, milling and stone, and I got none of them. Richard Moor of Stannick offered 6 coin for a copper tool, so copper tools are worth a great deal. DEBTS: Wilmot Cotter owes me 1 meat (agreement A20, in arrears; it was due by the end of autumn). Collect it when we meet. ROUTES: Holloway to the Weald is 1 day by cart track (a spring on the way). The Weald to Wynford is 1 more day by cart track; there is no direct road from Holloway to Wynford. High Tor is 1 day away, and Stannick is 1 day beyond it. A deer path runs north into deep woods (unexplored). Charcoal needs 5 timber a burn. The handcart carries 40 weight on a cart track and only 10 off it. WINTER PLAN: Stay home. Make a crude tool, fell timber, gather firewood, and keep the hearth fed. Burn charcoal from spare timber for spring trade. Don't travel in the cold unless it's needed: a night out costs 2 food.
